taxonomic_note: Current Kew POWO accepts Cercis canadensis subsp. mexicana; the Master Plant Pool's var. mexicana name is a synonym.
look_here_first: Mexican redbud is the smaller, more xeric-looking redbud: leaves are relatively small, thick, glossy, and characteristically wavy-edged, on a compact multi-trunked tree or large shrub.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kew gives the native range as southwestern Texas to northeastern Mexico. NPSOT places the Texas plant in Chihuahuan Desert/Stockton Plateau settings; historical botanical treatments place Texas occurrences from Crockett and Val Verde counties westward into the Trans-Pecos. No project target-zone native county was locked in B085.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Landscape plantings in Central Texas do not count as native range evidence.

best_field_traits: small multi-trunked tree or large shrub
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with Texas redbud, Mexican redbud usually has smaller, more strongly wavy-edged leaves and a more southwestern xeric distribution.
